newsitem.title: USA: Major stock market movements overnight - July 4.
newsitem.headline: Major stock market movements overnight - July 4.

text.p: NEW YORK - The Dow Jones industrial average leaped more than 100 points to close at a record high Thursday as the June employment report confirmed the economy is slowing at a pace that would keep the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates.

Based on early and unofficial data, the Dow ended up 100.43 points, or 1.29 percent, at 7,895.81, eclipsing its June 20 record close of 7,796.51. In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 19-7 on volume of 378 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The market closed early at 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT prior to Friday's Independence Day holiday.

LONDON - Shares gyrated wildly, plunging at the outset but then rebounding to record peaks despite the view that Wednesday's budget would lead to sharply higher interest rates. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,831.7, up 80.3 points, or 1.69 percent.

FRANKFURT - Share prices rose to drive the IBIS DAX index to a new all-time high of 3,944.34 in late trade, with dealers' sights firmly set on breaking the 4,000 level in the coming weeks. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,887.39, up 32.63 points, or 0.85 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index
ended at 3,939.73, up 72.20 points, or 1.87 percent.

PARIS - Shares closed almost one percent up, on the back of U.S. employment data which confirmed the bullish mood in the Paris market, traders said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,936.98, up 27.53 points, or 0.95 percent.
ZURICH - Shares leapt two percent to end above 5,800 points in the blue-chip SMI for the first time. The Swiss market index closed at 5,804.9, up 130.6 points, or 2.30 percent.

MILAN - Shares closed below the highs as investors took profits on telecom stocks although banks were still at the centre of attention while a record run on the bond market gave added support. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,603, up 109 points, or 0.81 percent.
AMSTERDAM - Shares began the day firmer and staged a further strong advance after positively received U.S. labour market data. The AEX index closed at 897.10, up 18.08 points, or 2.06 percent.
TOKYO - Stocks drifted in negative territory for most of Thursday's session and ended slightly lower. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,121.41, down 75.01 points, or 0.37 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks slumped on their first trading day under Chinese rule, unable to retain the momentum of an early surge to record highs as worries about the property market stamped out handover optimism. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,055.74, down 141.05 points, or 0.93 percent.

SYDNEY - The share market closed a touch lower as profit-takers sold into early gains after the benchmark All Ordinaries index pushed past the 2,500 mark. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,742.9, down 3.0 points, or 0.11 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Gold shares finished up in quiet trade as some short-covering pushed gold share prices slightly higher ahead of U.S. Independence Day public holiday on Friday, dealers said.
